benchmark_progress: Directly implements the benchmark's 'Source registry and provenance core is reproducible, with acquisition recipes plus field-level source assertions, provenance, and confidence' description: a schema-validated source registry (publicgraph.registry), versioned/reproducible acquisition recipes executed by a retrying runner against an injectable Fetcher (publicgraph.recipes/runner/fetchers), and field-level provenance with numeric confidence and conflict detection (publicgraph.provenance). Bulk data expansion has not started -- only illustrative, explicitly-not-production-vetted example data is bundled, per the benchmark's 'before bulk data expansion' ordering.
objective_addressed: Build source registry + reproducible acquisition recipes + field assertions/provenance/confidence before bulk downloading national data.
repo_starting_state: TheRealSynth/PublicGraph-USA was a completely empty GitHub repository at mission start: 0 commits, 0 branches, no README, no spec docs. This mission created the repository's first commits. No base_sha/base_ref was available (mission file supplied neither, and the repo had no default branch to resolve one from); see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md 'Starting state'.
changes_summary: src/publicgraph/validation.py (new): dependency-free structural validator (type/required/enum/pattern/min-max/array-items/date formats) -- see scope_note for why this isn't the jsonschema package.
src/publicgraph/registry.py (new): Source dataclass, validate_source_dict, load_registry -- loads/validates every source JSON file, rejects duplicate ids.
src/publicgraph/recipes.py (new): Recipe/RecipeStep dataclasses, validate_recipe_dict, load_recipes -- validates recipes and cross-references source_id against a supplied Registry.
src/publicgraph/provenance.py (new): FieldAssertion dataclass, confidence_band, load_assertions, find_conflicts (groups by entity_id+field_name, surfaces disagreeing values without auto-resolving).
src/publicgraph/fetchers.py (new): Fetcher protocol + stdlib-only HTTPFetcher (urllib), not exercised against live network by the test suite.

src/publicgraph/runner.py (new): run_recipe executes a Recipe's steps against any Fetcher, retries non-2xx responses up to retry_max_attempts, writes artifacts, returns ArtifactProvenance records (checksum, status, timestamp, attempts) per step.

src/publicgraph/data/sources/{census-acs,bls-cpi}.json (new): two illustrative example source registry entries, each explicitly marked 'not yet vetted for a production acquisition recipe' in their own notes field.
src/publicgraph/data/recipes/census-acs-homepage-probe.json (new): one illustrative recipe (fetches only the census-acs homepage, as a runner/fetcher pipeline smoke test, not a real dataset pull).

src/publicgraph/data/assertions/{census-acs-example,bls-cpi-example-conflict}.json (new): two synthetic (explicitly-not-real-data) example field assertions for the same fake entity/field with different values, to exercise find_conflicts.
tests/*.py (new, 8 files): 54 tests covering validation, registry, recipes, provenance, runner (with a fake Fetcher, no live network), and HTTPFetcher request/response handling (fully mocked).

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (new): design rationale, the empty-repo starting state, why the package has zero third-party dependencies given owns_paths, what was deliberately left out of scope, and proposed follow-up missions.
scope_note: owns_paths for this mission is src/**, tests/**, docs/** only -- no root-level files (README.md, a dependency manifest, .gitignore, CI config) could be added, matching the precedent set by mission TR-AI-REL-001 (TheRealSynth/ToolRefinery), which similarly dropped a useful change because it needed a root-level file outside its owns_paths. Two concrete effects: (1) this package deliberately has zero third-party dependencies -- publicgraph/validation.py hand-rolls the small JSON-Schema-like subset needed instead of depending on an undeclared/unpinned `jsonschema` package, and all data files are plain JSON rather than YAML, since neither could be pinned in a manifest this mission isn't scoped to create; (2) __pycache__/.pytest_cache directories generated while testing were deleted rather than gitignored, since a .gitignore is also outside owns_paths. A root-scoped follow-up mission should add README.md, a dependency manifest, and .gitignore. Full rationale in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

tests.unit: python3 -m pytest tests/ -q -- 54 tests, all passing, 8 files (test_validation, test_registry, test_recipes, test_provenance, test_runner, test_fetchers). Verified via a fresh run immediately before this commit.
tests.compile: python3 -m py_compile src/publicgraph/*.py -- clean, no errors.
tests.acceptance_commands: Mission file's acceptance.commands is an empty list; no mission-specified acceptance commands existed to run.

proposed_follow_ups: A root-scoped mission should add README.md, a dependency manifest (requirements.txt or pyproject.toml), .gitignore, and CI wiring to run pytest on every push/PR.
Once a dependency manifest exists, reassess whether to adopt jsonschema (more feature-complete than publicgraph/validation.py) and/or YAML for data files.

A source-specific mission should pick one real, narrow dataset (a single ACS table or BLS CPI series), confirm its actual API terms/rate limits/endpoint shape, and add a real (non-homepage-probe) acquisition recipe plus a first extraction pipeline producing real FieldAssertions.
Once two or more real sources assert the same fields, design and implement an actual conflict-resolution policy on top of find_conflicts().
owner_approvals_still_required: None of this mission's changes touch an owner_gate (no production deploy, DNS, billing, money movement, destructive migration, credential rotation, claim/outreach, signature, or contract acceptance). Per docs/PORTFOLIO_DASHBOARD.md in the control repo, this project's priority note says to 'continue national public-data normalization after CRS acquisition patterns stabilize' -- that is a portfolio-sequencing note, not a blocker on this already-claimed, already-in-owns_paths mission, but the owner may want to confirm before a follow-up mission proceeds to real data acquisition.
